<reason>A won by making the live comparison easier: kinetic tests are optional, highly verifiable debris, and B never showed a next-test benefit that outweighs a 2007-style cloud. B’s strongest attack—that the treaty cannot “prevent” cascades because mass and wartime intercepts remain—was blunted when A showed B’s own disposal/traffic rules share that hole and that a cascade is a threshold, so cutting deliberate fragments still counts. B stayed coherent on the motion’s verb but overclaimed sufficiency as the only valid test. Clipping cost A some polish, not the clash.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s questions on the next-test benefit and the shared wartime hole; B’s reply that a credential “does not have to outweigh” a debris cloud, which A then used as the decisive admission.</best_rebuttal>
